title: The Clock in the Chest, and a Rhythm That Clots

questions.stem: S T elevation, and this hospital can open the artery in the lab. A lytic in the parking lot?

options.text: Yes, always
No. Take them to the lab
Wait for the troponin first, then decide in an hour
Give oxygen to everyone, and stop

questions.explanation: A lytic is the backup when you will miss the clock, not the default at a ready lab.

questions.stem: A twelve-lead tracing in suspected heart-attack care is due:

options.text: Within ten minutes
After the troponin returns, always
The next day
Only if the saturation is low

questions.explanation: S T elevation does not wait for the troponin.

questions.stem: Oxygen in this chest-pain workup is for:

options.text: Every patient, because of the diagnosis
A low saturation, not the diagnosis itself
Replacing aspirin
Replacing the tracing

questions.explanation: If the saturation is already fine, routine oxygen is not the treatment.

questions.stem: Atrial fibrillation with a mechanical mitral valve. Which thinner?

options.text: A newer blood thinner, and stop warfarin
Warfarin
Aspirin alone
No thinner, because the valve is already there

questions.explanation: A mechanical valve, or significant mitral narrowing, still gets warfarin.

questions.stem: After a successful cardioversion in a patient who needed a thinner:

options.text: You can stop the thinner that week
Resetting the rhythm does not cancel the thinner
Aspirin becomes the substitute
The yearly risk no longer matters

questions.explanation: The indication is the risk, not today's tracing.

questions.stem: A dissection that involves the ascending aorta is:

options.text: A clinic problem for next month
An operation
Treated first with a clot-busting medicine
Treated first with a pure vessel-opener and no beta blocker

questions.explanation: A beta blocker comes before a pure vessel-opener. A lytic extends the tear.

options.text: A diuretic, as the definitive plan
Draining the fluid; a diuretic takes away needed preload
A nitrate plus an erection medicine
Watching overnight with no plan

questions.explanation: Fluids may bridge while drainage is arranged.

questions.stem: If you will miss the clock to open the artery, a clot-busting medicine is:

options.text: Never appropriate
The backup, if it is safe
Given in the parking lot of a ready lab anyway
A reason to skip the tracing

questions.explanation: About ninety minutes at a hospital that can open the artery, or two hours if the patient has to be moved.

questions.stem: Aspirin, in a suspected heart-attack workup without a reason to avoid it:

options.text: Is still indicated
Is replaced by routine oxygen
Is cancelled by atrial fibrillation
Waits for the troponin, like the lab activation
S T elevation does not wait for the troponin.
Open the artery if you can; a lytic is the backup when you will miss the clock.
Aspirin is the blood-thinner substitute in atrial fibrillation.
Tamponade is drained, not diuresed.

questions.explanation: Aspirin is not the substitute for anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
